explanations.text:
●  the server starts the watch                      ([start](start))
  │     The watch runs only in the ready-built program, the one
  │     install.sh puts on your machine. A copy of human made
  │     from the source code on your machine never updates itself.
  │     It does this for one reason only: so a test copy stays the
  │     copy you made.
  │
  ●  the watch asks for news once an hour             ([watch](watch))
  │     It asks at the start, then once an hour. A failed ask is
  │     kept as the reason and the watch tries again later.
  │
  ●  the watch reads the newest version               ([check](check))
  │     It reads https://downloads.doashuman.com/latest, a
  │     file that holds only a version, like 0.0.103. When that
  │     version is not newer than the one that runs, or than the
  │     one already downloaded, nothing more happens.
  │
  ●  the tool knows what runs                         ([version](version))
  │     It reads its own version. It also knows when it is the
  │     ready-built program ([frozen](frozen)), and which system
  │     and chip it runs on ([place](place)), like linux-arm64.
  │     It compares two versions number by number ([newer](newer)).
  │
  ●  the watch downloads the new version              ([download](download))
  │     It reads the list of the version, manifest.json, which
  │     names one file and one checksum for each system. It
  │     downloads the file of this system ([fetch](fetch)).
  │     When the checksum does not match, it stops and nothing
  │     changes on your machine.
  │     It unpacks the file into ~/.human/versions/<version>/.
  │
  ●  the watch puts the new version in place          ([activate](activate))
  │     The command human in ~/.local/bin now points at the new
  │     version ([program](program)), so every next command runs
  │     it. The server that runs keeps the old one until the
  │     restart. On windows the old program is moved aside,
  │     because windows does not let a running program be replaced.
  │
  ●  the watch deploys the skills again
  │     The new version copies its skills to your agent, so the
  │     skills always match the program.
  │     Then the server marks the new version as ready, and the
  │     reader shows the update button ([status](status)).
  │
  ●  you click the button, the server waits           ([restart_when](restart_when))
        The server waits until no compile runs and no writing
        waits for claude in any project. Then it closes its port
        and starts the new version with the same port, and the
        page loads again by itself.

──────
  ●  a copy from pypi says that human moved           ([from_pypi](from_pypi))
        A human installed with uv from pypi prints, at each
        command: human moved: curl -fsSL https://doashuman.com/install.sh | bash
